chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the Muhrim (person in Ihram) seek shade from the sun? He said: No, unless he is an old man. And he said: This is the reason.

key_terms.المُحرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.شَيخاً كَبِيراً: An old man, implying weakness or inability to endure heat

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim in Ihram use an umbrella or seek shade from the sun?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on seeking shade during Ihram, distinguishing between general prohibition and the concession for the elderly (*shaykh kabir*) due to physical weakness. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-'illah* (the underlying cause), where the exemption is granted not merely by age but by the specific need or frailty associated with it, balancing ritual purity with human comfort.
